subject: On-prem IaC composition and traffic policy review
messages:
From: AcmeCorp Infra <infra-team@acmecorp.com>

Cc: Stanley Ortiz <s.ortiz@edgecloud.io>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem IaC composition & traffic policy review
Attachments: network-diagram.png; iac-layout-v2.tf

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this. We are preparing a private deployment of Redwood for our internal ML workloads in our colo facility (rack-space A3). The attached diagram and the TF layout are a first pass. Can your team review the following and call out gaps / must-fix items from an IaC and network-policy perspective?

1) Composition: We have separate terraform modules for network (vlan/bgp), compute (baremetal provisioning), and infra-services (bastion, registry). Helm charts are an umbrella chart for Redwood services; Ansible is used for post-provision configuration. We want clear owner boundaries and a recommended directory structure so we can split responsibilities across our infra and platform teams.

2) Traffic policy: Ingress should be TLS passthrough to the model-serving nodes where possible; egress should be restricted to a small whitelist (model registries, metrics endpoints, KMS); we also need a plan for NTP/DNS and remote patching.

3) CI/CD gating: We will gate merges with network validation jobs. We need suggested pipeline jobs that are safe to run in the MR (non-destructive smoke) vs jobs that require test infra.

We are on a tight timeline (pilot in 3 weeks). Happy to hop on a call — proposing Mon May 10 14:00 PT if you need a synchronous review.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin (on behalf of Acme Infra)
infra-team@acmecorp.com

---
Forwarding: initial TF layout + network diagram attached for context.

Subject: Re: On-prem IaC composition & traffic policy review

Marcus — thanks for the detailed packet. I did a first pass and listed the most urgent gaps that would block pilot gating. Below are the high-level findings; I'll assign internal owners and we can expand into a MR review checklist.

High-level triage (blocking/major/minor):
- BLOCKING: Egress whitelist is too permissive -> needs explicit destination hosts/ips and signed justification for each entry (SOC2 ask). We should default to deny and add allow rules in a single source-controlled list.
- MAJOR: Helm umbrella chart currently assumes cluster networking (K8s CNI) semantics that don't hold for your baremetal topology (no kube-proxy / ipvs); we need to validate service IP allocation and headless service behavior for TLS passthrough.
- MAJOR: Secrets flow: Ansible playbooks reference plaintext files for KMS bootstrap; switch to vault-agent + KMS-wrapped secrets and ensure CI jobs do not print secrets.
- MINOR: Bastion ownership and logging — who rotates keys, where are SSH session logs forwarded?

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) Owner mapping: Karthik -> Terraform module boundaries & MR gating; Vanessa -> Helm/Ansible composition and runtime validation; Marissa -> evidence artifacts and SOC2 checklist alignment.
2) CI pipeline: Add a non-destructive 'network-validate' job to MR that runs a linter + local assert scripts against a template env (does not call cloud). Add a separate 'canary-deploy' job that runs in a sandbox project with explicit approvals.
3) Egress: Provide a CSV of required egress endpoints with CIDR, purpose, owner. We'll run a minimal whitelist by default.

I attached a short checklist that I'll use to review your MR (see related link to MR). If this looks right I can draft comments on MR #312 and we can iterate — otherwise we can take the Mon slot.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, AcmeCorp Infra <infra-team@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-06T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem IaC composition & traffic policy review

+1 to Neha's notes. A few concrete, tactical items from the Helm and Ansible side you can action quickly: 

Helm / runtime considerations:
- Helm umbrella chart: split the umbrella into two logical charts: control-plane (console, metrics, tracing) and data-plane (model-server, tokenizer workers). This keeps values matrices small and gives safer upgrade boundaries.
- TLS passthrough: For headless services we will rely on hostPort mapping or a lightweight L4 proxy on the node (envoy in transparent proxy mode) — not typical K8s Ingress. Add a node-level systemd unit (declarative via Ansible) that registers L4 listeners.
- helm-values-edge.yaml: add explicit `networkPolicy` stubs per release channel (prod/stage) and include a `egressWhitelist` list that the chart reads and renders into iptables rules. Do NOT bake secrets into values; use valueFrom / external secret references.

Ansible / post-provision security:
- Replace plaintext KMS bootstrap files with an Ansible role that retrieves secrets from HashiVault or KMS and injects ephemeral credentials with a short TTL.
- SSH bastion: enforce `ForceCommand` wrapper to capture sessions and forward logs to our central collection (splunk/graylog). Rotate keys via a CI-driven job weekly during the pilot.

Network / traffic policy details:
- Egress: only allow IPs for pkg registries, metrics endpoints, KMS, DNS, NTP. Block all  outbound 0.0.0.0/0 on application nodes; allow NAT from dedicated egress hosts.
- Ingress: for TLS passthrough, terminate TLS at the service if SNI routing required; otherwise use L4 pass-through and ensure clients use mutual TLS. Document fallback to TLS-terminate at L7 for telemetry endpoints.
- BGP / VLANs: Ensure Terraform module exposes `bgp_asn` and `vlan_id` as required variables and creates clear naming tags for route-objects so we can map back to billing.

CI suggestions (MR-safe jobs):
- mr/lint-iac (tfsec, terrascan, helm lint) — MR only
- mr/network-assert (static check: validate egress list format + IP allowlist) — MR only
- ci/staging-canary (applies in isolated sandbox project after manual approval) — needs runbook attached
- ci/egress-assertion (integration test in sandbox that attempts controlled egress to real endpoints) — gated

I attached a short sample `helm-values-edge.yaml` and a small systemd unit example for L4 proxy.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Platform Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

On the egress whitelist: please provide owners for each external host. Without owners we will enforce default deny for any entries missing justification.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: On-prem IaC composition & traffic policy review

Thanks — a few concrete Terraform layout suggestions that map to Vanessa/Neha's asks:

Proposed repo layout (short):
- modules/network/ -> vlan.tf, bgp.tf, firewall.tf (outputs: vpc_id, egress_nat_ip, bgp_session)
- modules/compute/ -> baremetal_provisioner.tf, host_inventory.tf (outputs: node_list, mac_map)
- services/helm/ -> umbrella control-plane + data-plane charts (values overriden per env)
- ansible/roles/ -> bastion, l4-proxy, kms-bootstrap

Terraform module boundaries / ownership:
- Acme Infra owns modules/network and modules/compute (because they control colo), Redwood owns services/helm and ansible roles that configure runtime. Shared variables only in a top-level `env.tfvars` to avoid duplication.

Example CI gating snippet (GitLab CI YAML fragment):
```yaml
stages:
  - lint
  - mr-validate
  - deploy

mr-validate:
  stage: mr-validate
  script:
    - terraform init -backend=false
    - terraform validate -check-variables=false
    - ./scripts/validate-egress-csv.sh $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID
  only:
    - merge_requests
  tags:
    - shell
```

MR gating policy: any change to `modules/network` requires at least two approvals (Acme infra + Redwood network), and `ci/staging-canary` must be green before merging into `main`. I can own the terraform gating and will open MR comments on #312 with these checks.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
